PART 1. Introduction
Strategic planning and programming is the cornerstone of the
management framework. The -2029 translates the
political priorities set in the Political Guidelines of President von der Leyen into general objectives.
This process ensures institutional coherence, enhances accountability, and aligns the actions of
all Commission departments with the strategic vision of the mandate.
Within this framework, each Commission service has developed a strategic outlook for 2025-
2029 in Management plan 2025. This outlook establishes a set of multiannual objectives and
indicators to measure progress towards their achievement. These will be used for planning and
reporting on performance throughout the period.
The 2026 management plan sets out what the Directorate-General for Justice and Consumers
(DG JUST) intends to deliver this year to contribute to these multiannual objectives (Part 2). It
also describes how DG JUST will contribute to the common objective of building a modern and
sustainable public administration (Part 3). The main outputs with their indicators and targets are
presented in Annexes 1 and 2. The chart below illustrates the performance framework for DG
JUST.

priorities in 2026
This part sets out the main expected deliverables that DG JUST plans to deliver in 2026. For
more details on the deliverables please see the performance tables in Annex 1 on page 28.
General
sustainable prosperity and competitiveness (1)
Specific objective 1.1: Improved conditions for companies,
including SMEs, through EU company law and corporate
governance rules, to set up, attract investment and grow
sustainably in the Single Market
As announced in the Commission Work Programme, the Commission will propose a 28th Regime
for Innovative Companies, which will simplify the applicable rules and reduce the cost of
failure, including as regards any relevant aspects of corporate, insolvency, labour and tax law.
The 28th regime will provide a single set of rules, potentially in a progressive and modular way
and will include an EU corporate legal framework. The adoption of the new Insolvency Directive
will contribute to the future regime in the field of insolvency.
As part of the continuous stress-testing of the acquis and as a contribution to the
goal to reduce administrative burdens, DG JUST will also evaluate and revise the
Shareholder Rights Directive to harmonise and simplify interactions between issuing
companies, their investors and intermediaries, and to reduce costs and burdens on those players
in the financial market.
DG JUST will develop guidelines and accompanying measures to support the implementation of
Directive 2024/1760 on Corporate sustainability due diligence (the deadline for
transposition is 26 July 2027 and the Directive will apply from 26 July 2028), subject to the
timelines decided as part of the Omnibus I legislation. DG JUST will adopt an implementing act
and support the transposition of Directive 2025/25 on Upgrading digital company law (the
first transposition deadline is 31 July 2027).
To further enable data-driven business models and the use of innovative technologies in the
digital economy by EU companies, the Commission will continue its work on adapting contract
law to the needs of the digital economy. Following the adoption of the Communication approving
the text on 19 November 2025, in 2026 DG JUST will prepare for adoption a Commission
Recommendation with model contract terms for access and use of data and standard

contractual clauses for cloud computing contracts (in all EU official languages). The model
contractual terms will help SMEs, in particular, to navigate their obligations, reduce legal
complexity and focus on innovation. This Commission Recommendation is based on Article 41 of
the Data Act. From 2026, DG JUST will closely monitor the uptake- of the model contractual
terms and will review, complement or adapt them if necessary in line with international
developments in data sharing.
Under the Apply AI strategy (action on AI contracting is outlined in the Annex III) DG JUST will set
up a discussion forum with interested stakeholders on reducing risks in AI contracting for SMEs
(including start-ups). It will provide legal guidance, notably in the form of model contract terms
for AI contracts and guidance on the choice of AI contracting systems. The Commission will also
consider the need for a contract terms data pool for automated contracting as mentioned in the
Data Union strategy.
Specific objective 1.2: The justice system is adapted to
digitalisation
In 2026, DG JUST will begin to implement the DigitalJustice@2030 strategy, adopted in
November 2025. The strategy aims to accelerate the digitalisation of national justice systems,
bringing forward efficiency gains, cost savings, and greater transparency and accessibility, which
are a precondition for economic growth and competitiveness.
In particular, and in line with the strategy, the Commission will create a living repository of
digital tools, in particular AI, used in justice systems across the EU. This would include good
solutions in use in the Member States that could be applied more widely and foster cross-border
interoperability. The repository should be available on the European e-Justice Portal by the end
of 2026. The repository will facilitate the exchange of best practices between the Member
States. At the same time, the Commission will create an IT Toolbox for Justice, which will be
hosted on the Interoperable Europe Portal, where Member States can include those IT (including
AI) tools that they are willing to share with each other.
Under the European Legal Data Space, DG JUST will reconvene the European Case Law Identifier
(ECLI) Expert Group, which will serve as a forum to discuss best practices and challenges in
making judicial data accessible online. In addition, work will begin on improving the ECLI search
engine on the European e-Justice Portal and implementing the ECLI extended standard.
As regards the use of videoconferencing in justice, the strategy has announced an initiative
on voluntary, common EU-wide technical requirements for videoconferencing by 2027, and that
by the end of 2027 it will study the feasibility and assess the costs and benefits of different
options to overcome interoperability issues in cross-border videoconferencing in judicial
proceedings. A study to prepare these initiatives will be launched in 2026.
The implementation of the Digitalisation Regulation will continue in 2026, with the adoption
of the implementing acts for the first batch of legal acts. The development of the reference
implementation software and the European Electronic Access Point will continue throughout the
year, with the adoption of the implementing act on Electronic Access Point planned for 2026.
8

The implementation of the new European Judicial Training Strategy will play a key role in
advancing the digital transition of justice systems across the EU. The 2026 European Judicial
Training Conference, organised under the auspices of Council of the
EU, will serve as the launch event of the Judicial Training Forum, which will aim to foster
results-oriented stakeholder engagement and outreach. A series of 40 training e-Capsules,
covering a broad range of EU criminal law, civil law, and fundamental rights topics, will be
available on the European Training Platform (ETP). The priorities of the 2026 calls for
proposals under the Justice programme for both projects and operating grants will be aligned
where relevant with the new digitalisation-related strategic objectives of the strategy.
Furthermore, the 2026 Judicial Training Report will establish clear benchmarks to assess
progress in digitalisation.
Digitalisation improves the efficiency and resilience of our justice systems and thus supports the
competitiveness of our economy, while also strengthening access to justice. However, this is a
costly process which requires significant investments.
2028-2034 multiannual financial framework (MFF) includes a stronger Justice programme
with a budget of nearly EUR 800 million (nearly three times the amount available under the
current MFF). The significant increase in the budget of the Justice Programme will allow for the
digitalisation of justice to progress at EU level, as one of objectives. The Justice
Programme will support the implementation of the two strategies the Digital Justice Strategy
and Judicial Training Strategy, while it will also continue to support the digitalisation of cross-
border judicial proceedings. Digitalisation of justice is also particularly challenging for already
strained national budgets. The proposed National and Regional Partnership Plans could offer
significant funding opportunities to support national digitalisation efforts.
General objective 2: A new era for European
defence and security (2)
Specific objective 2.1: Accountability ensured for Russia's war
of aggression against Ukraine and a more effective fight
against violations of EU restrictive measures
In 2026, DG JUST will continue to work on ensuring accountability for the crimes connected with
Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine, notably by supporting the preparations to
establish the Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression against Ukraine and the ongoing
work of the International Centre for the Prosecution of the Crime of Aggression (ICPA)
at Eurojust.
The Commission will also continue to support the creation of a compensation mechanism for
Ukraine, which includes continuing participating in the Register of Damage, joining the

International Claims Commission, and contributing to the design of the future compensation
fund with international partners.
DG JUST will continue to strengthen coordination within the EU and with international partners in
enforcing EU restrictive measures (sanctions) and combating their violations, notably
through the Freeze and Seize Task Force, in close cooperation with the Directorates-General
for Financial Stability, Financial Services and Capital Markets Union (DG FISMA), Migration and
Home Affairs (DG HOME), and Taxation and Customs Union (DG TAXUD).
Additionally, DG JUST will also continue its work to ensure a more effective fight against
violations of EU restrictive measures (sanctions), including by means of criminal law. In
2026, DG JUST will continue supporting Member States in the correct and complete transposition
of Directive 2024/1226 on the criminalisation of sanctions violations (the transposition
deadline expired on 20 May 2025). To this end, it will consider the appropriate measures to take
as a follow up to the ongoing infringement cases for non-communication of transposition
measures and will carry out conformity checks of the measures taken by the Member States to
transpose this Directive into their national systems.
General objective 3: Supporting people, and
strengthening our societies and our social
models (3)
Specific objective 3.1: Fighting discrimination and promoting
equality for all (4)
In 2026, the Commission will continue its efforts to build a Union of Equality, including by raising
awareness of EU action to promote equality and fight discrimination through a communication
campaign to engage people across the EU.
As announced in the Commission Work Programme, the Commission will adopt the new Gender
equality strategy 2026-2030. It will build on the , adopted
in March 2025, and the eight principles for a gender-equal society outlined in its annexed
Declaration, which have been endorsed by all Member States, EU institutions and over 50 EU-
level and international stakeholders. The Roadmap will inform the concrete policy actions of the
new Gender Equality Strategy addressing all issues affecting women, from the fight against
gender-based violence to the economic empowerment of women, their participation in politics
and addressing discrimination in health, education, housing, social protection and in the supply

DG JUST will support the implementation of the Directive on Combating violence against
women and domestic violence by organising workshops. Further support will also be provided
for the implementation of the Pay Transparency Directive with the development of tools to
help companies apply the new rules. DG JUST will also continue to assess the compliance of
national legislation transposing the Directive on Work-Life Balance which had to be
transposed by August 2022 and August 2024.
DG JUST will intensify its work on tackling cyber violence against women by working with
internet platforms to develop a code of conduct on gender-based cyber violence. This
work will follow-up on a high-level event with platforms which took place in November 2025. DG
JUST will also continue to support the evaluation of the the Istanbul
Convention by GREVIO, the Group of Experts on Action against Violence against Women and
Domestic Violence.
As also announced in the Commission Work Programme, in 2026 DG JUST will present a
Communication on Enhancing the Strategy for the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
up to 2030. Halfway through the implementation of the ten-year strategy adopted in 2021, the
Commission will aim to reinforce it to further foster disability rights in the EU and beyond. The
Communication is set to put forward new actions under the strategy up to 2030. A progress
report will accompany the Communication.
In parallel, DG JUST will continue to implement the strategy by, for example: (i) supporting the
implementation by the EU of the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with
Disabilities; (ii) supporting the implementation of the Directive establishing the European
Disability Card and European Parking Card for persons with disabilities, including by
producing delegated and implementing acts; (iii) supporting the transposition of the European
Accessibility Act and setting up an expert group to facilitate cooperation and exchanges of
information between authorities and stakeholders on matters related to the implementation of
the Act; and (iv) organising the European Day of Persons with Disabilities and the Access
City Award.
DG JUST will focus on making progress in the negotiations on the proposal for the equal
treatment Directive, by supporting the Council Presidency and Member States in reaching an
agreement.
In 2026, DG JUST will prioritise implementing the LGBTIQ+ equality strategy 2026-2030 to
protect LGBTIQ+ people from violence, empower them to live free from discrimination and on an
equal footing with all other individuals. Key actions include combating conversion practices,
fighting hate crimes and hate speech, and ensuring funding for civil society organisations that
are fighting for LGBITQ+ equality.
11

DG JUST will also prepare a reply to the 'Ban on conversion practices in the European Union'
initiative, which was submitted to the European Commission on 17 November and presented to
Commissioner Lahbib on 12 December 2025. It will also draw on a study analysing the
phenomenon to shape future actions and support Member States in banning these practices. DG
JUST will consider a legislative initiative to fight effectively hate offences committed online,
which would tackle LGBTIQ+-phobic cyber harassment, violence or hatred.
Additionally, DG JUST will promote a new LGBTIQ+ Policy Forum to engage LGBTIQ+ civil
society organisations, social partners, and researchers to address emerging challenges, and
monitor progress.
In 2026, DG JUST will continue its coordination work with Member States on equality and
discrimination within the High-Level Group on Non-Discrimination, Equality, and Diversity.
In 2026, the high-level group will also focus on improving the collection and analysis of equality
data. This work is essential for evidence-based policies with an intersectional approach.
Additionally, a second High-Level European Round Table on Equality Data will be organised
to bring together key stakeholders and further promote the collection and use of equality data.
The Task Force on Equality supports the Commissioner for Equality and consists of a network
of representatives from all departments of the Commission and the European External Action
Service. In 2026, the Task Force will strive to implement effective equality mainstreaming in the
Commission so that equality considerations are integrated into EU policies, legislation and
funding programmes. DG JUST and the Secretariat-General will support the network.
In 2026, work will continue to promote diversity and inclusion at the workplace through the EU
Platform of Diversity Charters. DG JUST will continue to cooperate with the Diversity
Charters to prepare guidance, for instance, on inclusive hiring practices. In addition, the
Commission will organise the 5th edition of the European Capitals of Inclusion and
Diversity Award and the 7th edition of the EU Diversity Month to recognise best practices
in creating diverse and discrimination-free communities and workplaces. In 2026, a specific
award and the theme of the Diversity Month are dedicated to 'an inclusive labour market for
all'.
In 2026, DG JUST will continue its efforts to counter racism effectively by adopting the first Anti-
Racism Strategy 2026-2030, which will be presented at the Anti-racism conference that is
being organised together with the Cypriot presidency and will take place in March. DG JUST will
also continue to monitor the correct application of EU antidiscrimination legislation and will adopt
a report on the application of the Racial Equality and Employment Equality Directives.
DG JUST will further support the Member States in their transposition of the Directives on
standards for equality bodies, which must be completed by June 2026, through expert group
meetings, guidance and an online space. It will also adopt an implementing act with a list of
common indicators on the functioning of equality bodies.
The reformed EU Roma strategic framework sets a number of targets until 2030 that aim to
promote effective equality, socio-economic inclusion and the meaningful participation of Roma
in society. As part of its implementation, the Commission will adopt a report on the
12

implementation of national Roma strategic frameworks and continue to monitor Roma
civil society. DG JUST will work closely with the Member States to facilitate the implementation
of their national Roma strategic frameworks and it will support activities that promote positive
narratives and Roma role models, combat negative stereotypes, raise awareness of Roma history
and culture, and promote truth and reconciliation under the Citizens, Equality, Rights and Values
(CERV) programme. DG JUST will also organise the 19th European Platform for Roma
Inclusion (EPRI) in cooperation with the Irish Presidency in October 2026.
DG JUST will continue to fund projects and organisations active in the area of equality and non-
discrimination via the CERV programme. In its proposal for the next MFF (2028-2034), the
Commission proposed a new funding programme which will bring together support for culture,
media and rights and values AgoraEU. The CERV+ strand of the new programme will continue
to support equality and non-discrimination initiatives.
As part of continuous stress-testing of the acquis, DG JUST will organise a reality check back-
to-back with an implementation dialogue on the European Care Strategy.
Specific objective 3.2: Consumers are empowered and better
protected (5)
2026 will mark the first year of implementation of the 2030 Consumer Agenda and the
Action Plan for Consumers on the Single Market, adopted in November 2025. In 2026, DG
JUST will organise three flagship events in the consumer policy area: the European Consumer
Summit, the Ministerial Meeting on Consumer Policy (organised together with the Irish
Presidency), and the International Product Safety Week.
DG JUST will also continue to stress test consumer policy. A new Implementation Dialogue will
be organised in 2026 to get feedback from stakeholders in view of facilitating the
implementation of policies and the simplification of rules. In addition, DG JUST will organise the
2026 edition of the Youth Policy Dialogue on consumer policy, with the participation of
Commissioner McGrath, to engage young people and youth organisations in shaping consumer
policy and to ensure that the perspectives of the younger generations are reflected in policy
discussions.
As announced in the Commission Work Programme, the adoption of the proposal for the Digital
Fairness Act (DFA) is planned for early autumn 2026. The DFA will address the problems such
as (i) dark patterns that can unfairly influence consumer decisions; (ii) addictive designs that
incentivise consumers to keep using a service or spend more money; (iii) problematic
commercial practices of social media influencers; (iv) unfair personalisation practices;
and (v) issues with digital contracts and subscriptions. The protection of minors will be

a key priority. The DFA will also clarify and simplify the existing rules where possible, without
compromising the high level of consumer protection.
DG JUST will prepare the implementation report on the the Digital Content Directive (EU)
2019/770 and the Sale of Goods Directive (EU) 2019/771 by the end of 2026.
DG JUST will also focus on the timely and correct transposition of Directive 2024/1799 on
promoting the repair of goods. We will continue to support Member States in implementing
the directive and will organise at least one workshop on its transposition. In addition, DG JUST
plans to adopt a second Commission delegated directive to update Annex II to the Directive.
Following its February 2025 Communication A comprehensive EU toolbox for safe and
sustainable e- , the Commission announced in the 2030 Consumer Agenda the
revision of the Consumer Protection Cooperation (CPC) Regulation (EU) 2017/2394 as
one of the measures needed to strengthen enforcement and address the challenges of e-
commerce. The adoption of a proposal for a revised CPC Regulation is planned for early autumn
2026, potentially together with the DFA. The main objective of this initiative is to make
enforcement more effective to , especially in the context of large-
scale infringements of consumer law, and to contribute to ensuring a fairer level-playing field for
compliant traders in the EU.
Throughout 2026, the Commission will work with Member States and stakeholders to facilitate
the correct and timely implementation of the revised Directive on Alternative Dispute
Resolution. DG JUST will organise transposition workshops for competent authorities and launch
the digital tool to inform consumers on redress mechanisms. A call for grants will be launched
with an envelope of EUR 1.5 million targeting both Alternative Dispute Resolution entities and
qualified entities under the Representative Actions Directive to improve their infrastructure,
capacity building, digitalisation and awareness raising.
DG JUST will continue to strongly support the European Consumer Centres (ECC-Net) to
further consolidate their capacity to advise and assist consumers when they encounter problems
with cross-border transactions.
DG JUST will oversee the implementation of key legislative files adopted in 2023 2024,
including the Consumer Credit Directive, the Distance Marketing of Financial Services
Directive and the Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition Directive. Work will
focus on supporting Member States in the transposition and enforcement of these instruments,
providing guidance to ensure consistent interpretation, and promoting the uptake of (new)
consumer rights, in particular as regards information on product durability and the reminder of
the existing legal guarantee. DG JUST will also begin to support Member States in transposing
the revised Package Travel Directive (EU) 2015/2302 (which aims to make the protection of
travellers more effective), in particular by organising transposition workshops.
DG JUST will further strengthen its role in supporting and coordinating actions of the
Consumer Protection Cooperation (CPC) Network to tackle widespread and cross-border
breaches of consumer legislation in key market sectors. The focus will remain on unfair
commercial practices and unfair contract terms in digital and e-commerce environments, as well
as on misleading environmental claims and other issues related to sustainable consumption.
14

DG JUST will also design and coordinate the yearly large-scale thematic consumer law
compliance screenings ( sweep ) of EU and non-EU traders, as well as the second product
safety sweep stemming from the General Product Safety Regulation (GPSR). DG JUST will
continue to support digitalisation and the use of AI in consumer enforcement.
DG JUST will continue a wide range of activities to support the effective implementation of the
Representative Actions Directive (EU) 2020/1828, by increasing the operational capacity of
qualified entities that are enabled to carry out the representative actions and by strengthening
cooperation between -
REACT, a restricted internet platform run by DG JUST, will continue to facilitate the cross-border
cooperation among these actors. DG JUST will continue to carry out transposition checks,
including opening EU dialogues with Member States and, if needed, non-conformity infringements
proceedings.
In the field of product safety, the Commission will continue to fully support the implementation
and enforcement of the GPSR, which took effect on 13 December 2024 and provides an updated
EU framework for general product safety. In the framework of stress-testing the acquis, a
General Product Safety Regulation reality check through the GPSR Businesses Sounding
Board is planned in November 2026. Among other things, this Reality Check will help get input
illegal online content by end 2027. We will also actively contribute to the work on the review of
the Market Surveillance Regulation to make product safety enforcement more efficient.
In 2026, DG JUST will organise the largest coordinated activities for product safety (CASP) to
date, covering 11 activities ad amounting to EUR 5,000,000, which will focus on many new
aspects that market surveillance authorities have asked for. In 2026 DG JUST will finalise a study
on e-vulnerability, an ongoing CASP activity on mental health and continue the work with OECD
on the risks posed by new technology products.
Additionally, and to be able to continue monitoring the ever-increasing threat of dangerous
products entering our Single Market, DG JUST will actively incorporate AI technologies into the
Safety Gate Rapid Alert System for dangerous non-food products. The Commission will
also further enhance the eSurveillance WebCrawler. The IT application developed by the European
Commission detects products that have been notified in Safety Gate and are still sold or reappear
in web shops and online marketplaces.
On the international scene, fforts will also focus on improving cooperation to
enhance global product safety, tackling product safety at the source and aiming to increase
product safety globally. Initiatives with international partners like Canada, China, the UK, and
the US are ongoing. DG JUST will carry on its work with partner organisations like the OECD, and
UNCTAD, including by funding studies and workshops. DG JUST will continue the EU-Japan
Informal Dialogue on Consumer Policy, fostering exchanges on sustainability, digitalisation and
vulnerable consumers. DG JUST will also remain an active member of the OECD Consumer Policy
Committee (CCP).
At operational level, DG JUST will monitor and support EU-funded projects promoting debt advice
and consumer education, helping citizens to build financial resilience and make responsible
economic decisions. The Consumer Data Dashboard will be operational in 2026, providing an
15

interactive, data-driven overview of key consumer indicators, and insights into market
developments and consumer conditions across the EU.
General objective 5: Protecting our democracy,
upholding our values (6)
Specific objective 5.1: Strengthened rule of law in the EU
DG JUST will continue to develop and apply all the instruments in the rule of law toolbox to
prevent challenges from emerging and address concerns where they arise. DG JUST together with
SG as co-lead service will further consolidate the Annual Rule of Law Report at the centre of
an integrated annual rule of law cycle with a common rhythm, clear milestones, and contributions
from all institutions. The focus will be on closing the existing loopholes, also in view of the
challenges identified in the Rule of Law Report. The single market dimension of the Rule of Law
Report introduced in 2025 will be further expanded on. Enlargement countries will be included in
the Rule of Law cycle if and when they are ready. DG JUST will also contribute to the on-going
work on strengthening the link between respect for the rule of law and EU funds, in particular in
the context of the negotiations on the next Multiannual Financial Framework.
DG JUST will further develop the Annual EU Justice Scoreboard, and its comparative overview
of the efficiency, quality, and independence of national justice systems, including the indicators
relevant for the single market.
Specific objective 5.2: Strengthened application of
fundamental rights
DG JUST will continue to strengthen the application of the EU Charter of Fundamental
Rights, ensuring a high level of data protection throughout the EU, combating hate speech and
relevant policies within the EU and internationally.
DG JUST will start implementing the actions presented in the EU Strategy for Civil Society,
adopted in November 2025. The Strategy has set up a
engagement with civil society and to take measures to protect and support civil society
organisations and human rights defenders in their day-to-day activities, including through
funding. In 2026, DG JUST will set up a Civil Society Platform to better facilitate dialogue with
civil society organisations that work in the area of EU values and rights, specifically those that
work to uphold fundamental rights, democracy and the rule of law.
In 2026, the Commission will present its annual report on the application of the EU Charter

Targeted amendments to the EUDPR will be prepared in the context of the Criminal Law package.
DG JUST will further harmonise and consolidate the data protection regime for processing of
operational personal data by JHA agencies.
To continue to promote safe and free data flows with international partners, DG JUST
should use and further develop all the available transfer tools adapted to different situations
and legal frameworks. To this end, the existing sets of Standard Contractual Clauses should be
